bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar to set up 44 hi-tech sugarcane nurseries with subsidy of up to Rs 11.25 lakh each
bihar_raw_news.content: All News English Indian Sugar News Sugar News Bihar is planning to establish 44 hi-tech sugarcane nurseries to promote cultivation and ensure the availability of quality, disease-free planting material to farmers across the state, Amar Ujala reported. The Sugarcane Industries Department has introduced the scheme for the first time, with a target of producing around 2.20 crore improved and disease-free sugarcane seedlings annually through the proposed nurseries. Each nursery is expected to produce around five lakh seedlings a year using the single-bud plantlet technique. Work is progressing at four locations. One nursery is being established in Patna district and another in Jamui, while two more have been approved in Muzaffarpur district. Bihar currently has around 2.25 lakh hectares under sugarcane cultivation. The department aims to expand cultivation, particularly in areas that are not served by sugar mills. The availability of quality planting material is also expected to support the proposed establishment of 25 new sugar mills and the revival of closed mills, which will require a reliable supply of sugarcane. The scheme also aims to increase farmers’ income through local nursery operations and create employment opportunities for rural youth and women. The nurseries will be developed under a public-private partnership model. Progressive farmers, JEEViKA groups, farmer-producer organisations, self-help groups, private entrepreneurs, sugar mills and jaggery manufacturers are eligible to apply through the Bihar Cane Care portal. The estimated cost of setting up one nursery is Rs 15 lakh, taking the total cost for 44 nurseries to Rs 6.60 crore. The government will provide a subsidy of up to 75% of the project cost, subject to a maximum of Rs 11.25 lakh per nursery.

bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar Museum beats the Louvre in Global Museum Rankings; Here's what makes it stand out
bihar_raw_news.content: Compiled By : Salma Sulthana Last Updated: 14 November 2026, 02:56 PM IST 5 min Share Follow us on Ranked ninth among the world's best museums in 2026, Bihar Museum in Patna offers ancient sculptures, Mithila art, historical treasures and contemporary exhibitions ❎ If the Louvre in Paris or the Metropolitan Museum of Art in New York is on your travel wish list, there is another museum you might want to visit before. The Bihar Museum ranked ninth on German travel guide Worth a Journey’s 2026 list of the world's 100 best museums. It stands one place above New York's famous Met, while the Louvre features at number 31. The ranking makes it the highest-placed museum in Asia and the only Indian institution on the list. To advertise here, Contact Us But the reason to make a trip here goes beyond its position on a global list. Spread across nearly 14 acres, the museum brings together archaeological treasures, ancient sculptures, regional art traditions and contemporary works. It offers a chance to explore Bihar's history and its influence on India's cultural landscape, all under one roof. Why Bihar deserves a place on your museum itinerary The museum's story began with a space problem. Patna Museum, established in 1917, had accumulated around 40,000 artefacts, but its galleries could display only a small part of the collection. The proposal to add more space eventually gave way to a much bigger idea: creating a modern museum that could present Bihar's history and artistic heritage to a wider audience. The result is the Bihar Museum, a 13.9-acre complex designed by Japanese architectural firm Maki and Associates in collaboration with Mumbai-based OPOLIS. Construction began in 2013, and the museum opened its first sections to visitors in August 2015. The remaining galleries followed in October 2017. The architecture is worth noticing before you even enter the galleries. Rather than one imposing block, the museum follows a campus-style layout, with different sections connected through walkways and open spaces. Weathering steel, stone, terracotta and glass give the buildings a contemporary appearance while drawing on materials associated with the region's history. What should you look out for inside? With more than 20,000 artefacts listed in its collection, the museum takes visitors through different periods of Bihar's history, from prehistoric times and ancient kingdoms to later cultural influences. The galleries are arranged thematically and chronologically, so there is plenty to explore even if you are not someone who usually spends an afternoon in a museum. Here are some of the sections worth making time for. The Didarganj Yakshi: If there is one exhibit you should not leave without seeing, it is this sculpture. Standing 5 feet 2 inches tall, the female figure is carved from Chunar sandstone and dates to the third century BCE. It was discovered on the banks of the Ganga at Didarganj, Patna, in 1917. bihar_raw_news.title: Mob vandalises Bihar hospital, sets ambulance ablaze after dispute turns violent
bihar_raw_news.content: Mob vandalises Bihar hospital, sets ambulance ablaze after dispute turns violent Written By : Medical Dialogues Team Published On 2026-11-14T12:44:22+05:30 | Updated On 14 Nov 2026 2:45 PM IST Aurangabad: In a shocking incident, an ambulance was set on fire, and a private hospital in Bihar's Aurangabad district was vandalised after a dispute over the treatment of a patient escalated into violence on Thursday. The incident led to a major law-and-order situation, with an angry mob also blocking a main road for nearly five hours. According to reports, the dispute reportedly began on Tuesday night after a disagreement arose over the treatment of a female patient suffering from severe anaemia. The hospital had advised shifting the patient to another facility, but a relative of another patient objected, saying he would arrange blood for her instead. The disagreement between the doctor and the patient's relative subsequently turned into a physical altercation. During the dispute, a 45-year-old man from Charkupa village was allegedly assaulted and sustained serious injuries . He was subsequently shifted to Patna for further treatment. His condition reportedly deteriorated on Thursday, and he went into a coma. News of his deteriorating condition reached nearby villages, triggering anger among his relatives and local residents. Also Read:Hospital staff attacked, property vandalised over treatment charges in Nagpur Tension escalated further after rumours circulated that the injured man had died. A large crowd gathered outside the private hospital and allegedly damaged the clinic premises. An ambulance was set on fire, while furniture and other items inside the facility were vandalised . The protesters also blocked the RafiGanj-Gaya main road, disrupting traffic for around five hours, Dainik Bhaskar reported. Fire brigade personnel who arrived to control the blaze reportedly faced opposition from the mob, forcing them to deal with the situation amid heightened tension. Senior police and administrative officials, along with additional security personnel, reached the spot and attempted to pacify the protesters. The road blockade was eventually lifted after several rounds of discussions between the administration and local representatives. Police said the doctor and the compounder had been taken into custody and that an investigation into the incident was underway. Authorities have maintained a watch in the area to prevent further unrest. The incident has raised concerns over the escalation of disputes inside healthcare facilities and the safety of medical staff, patients and hospital property during such confrontations. bihar_raw_news.title: Two Bihar boys rescued from bonded labour in Odisha receive first rehabilitation aid a year later
bihar_raw_news.content: The boys were allegedly made to work from 5 am to 10 pm without wages. Express Illustration Odisha Two Bihar boys rescued from bonded labour in Odisha receive first rehabilitation aid a year later The 12- and 14-year-olds, allegedly forced to work up to 17 hours a day at gupchup-making units in Ganjam, received Rs 30,000 each in October, against an entitlement of Rs 2 lakh apiece. Sisir Panigrahy Updated: 14th Nov, 2026 at 10:36 AM BERHAMPUR: For two young boys brought from Bihar to work in gupchup-making units in Ganjam’s Hinjilicut, being rescued from exploitation did not mean an immediate return of their childhood. Although they were freed in October 2025, their first instalment of rehabilitation assistance of Rs 30,000 each was released on October 23, 2026, nearly a year after their rescue. The boys, aged 12 and 14, are to get Rs 2 lakh each. The boys were allegedly made to work from 5 am to 10 pm without wages. They were reportedly beaten if they failed to meet sales targets and prevented from attending school or communicating with their families. Their parents were allegedly promised monthly wages and given advances of Rs 3,000 and Rs 5,000, respectively. On the eve of Children’s Day, their case highlights a larger concern in Odisha, where poverty and advance payments to parents can push children into conditions of bondage, while inadequate identification of such cases may deprive them of protection under the Bonded Labour System (Abolition) Act. Bonded child labour is not always recognised as distinct from ordinary child labour. If officials treat such cases only under general child labour provisions, children may miss the release and rehabilitation benefits available under the bonded labour legislation. Add as a preferred source on Google A case in Ganjam’s Chikiti block illustrates this gap. A boy was allegedly forced to graze buffaloes for nearly two years without wages and kept almost like a prisoner. He was rescued on September 1, 2026, and was declared a freed bonded labourer on September 10, making him eligible for rehabilitation assistance. However, after the child welfare committee handed him over to his parents, the employer allegedly took him away again. His parents reportedly alleged that the employer threatened them and demanded repayment of the money he claimed to have advanced to them. The boy was rescued a second time only after a police case was registered. Jajpur has demonstrated rehabilitation assistance can be delivered under the revised Rehabilitation of Bonded Labourer Scheme-2026. In September, it became the first district in Odisha to disburse assistance under the scheme. Eight children rescued during 2024-25 received financial assistance of Rs 40,000 each. Incidentally, two children were rescued from bonded labour in Jajpur on Friday. bihar_raw_news.title: Tigers to Be Relocated to Buxa Tiger Reserve from Assam and Bihar - Drishti IAS
bihar_raw_news.content: West Bengal Prev Next Tigers to Be Relocated to Buxa Tiger Reserve from Assam and Bihar 14 Nov 2026 5 min read Why in News? West Bengal has announced plans to relocate two more tigers from Assam and Bihar to Buxa Tiger Reserve (BTR) by the end of November 2026. The initiative aims to strengthen the reserve's resident tiger population as part of a phased tiger reintroduction and recovery programme. Key Points: Proposed Tiger Relocation Destination: Buxa Tiger Reserve, Alipurduar district, West Bengal. Source states: Assam and Bihar. Number of tigers: Two. Expected timeline: By the end of November 2026. Objective: To strengthen the resident tiger population and establish a viable, breeding and self-sustaining tiger population in Buxa. The relocation programme is being undertaken under the supervision of the National Tiger Conservation Authority (NTCA) . Earlier Relocation of a Tigress from Bihar On 2 October 2026 , a three-year-old tigress, identified as T138 , was released into Buxa Tiger Reserve. It was translocated from Valmiki Tiger Reserve, Bihar , marking the beginning of the phased tiger reintroduction programme. The tigress subsequently moved into Assam and was captured by forest personnel using a tranquilliser dart. It was brought back to Buxa on 4 November 2026 . Tiger Augmentation and Recovery Programme The tiger recovery initiative in Buxa has been implemented by the West Bengal Government with support from the NTCA and the Wildlife Institute of India (WII) . The collaborative recovery project has been underway since 2018 . Major interventions include: Prey-base augmentation: More than 800 chital have been released to improve prey availability. Habitat restoration: Approximately 380 hectares of grassland have been restored or converted over the past eight years. Scientific monitoring: Camera traps and telemetry are used to monitor tiger movement and population recovery. Protection measures: Strengthening anti-poaching activities and forest protection. Community participation: Engagement of 64 Eco-Development Committees and Joint Forest Management Committees. The programme aims to complement natural tiger recovery through scientifically guided interventions. Why Buxa Tiger Reserve Was Selected for Tiger Reintroduction Buxa experienced a prolonged absence of a stable resident tiger population due to: Habitat degradation and fragmentation. Changes in land use. Decline in prey availability. Increasing anthropogenic pressure. The reserve has ecological connectivity with Bhutan and adjoining forest landscapes of Assam . Camera-trap evidence has indicated natural tiger movement through the wider landscape, including an individual matched with a tiger from Manas Tiger Reserve, Assam , in 2023. About Buxa Tiger Reserve Location: Alipurduar district, West Bengal. Established as a Tiger Reserve: 1983, under Project Tiger. Area: Approximately 760.87 sq. km. Geographical significance: Located in the eastern Himalayan foothills and the Dooars region. Ecological connectivity: Linked with forest landscapes of Bhutan and Assam. Major rivers: Sankosh, Raidak, Jayanti and Torsa are associated with the wider landscape. Vegetation: Tropical moist and dry deciduous forests, along with other forest types. bihar_raw_news.title: Nitish Setu Inauguration Gets 35-Official Push Ahead of Modi Visit - Urban Acres
bihar_raw_news.content: Home Breaking News Nitish Setu Inauguration Gets 35-Official Push Ahead of Modi Visit Breaking News Nitish Setu Inauguration Gets 35-Official Push Ahead of Modi Visit By Maria Dsouza November 14, 2026 0 Copy URL Facebook Linkedin X WhatsApp Preparations for the inauguration of the six-lane Kachchi Dargah-Bidupur bridge, named Nitish Setu, have intensified ahead of Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s scheduled visit to Vaishali on November 21, with the Bihar government deploying 35 senior officials and the NDA organising booth-level mobilisation for the programme. Modi is scheduled to inaugurate the Jandaha-Rajapakar industrial area and formally dedicate the bridge across the Ganga to the public during the visit. The state government has named the bridge Nitish Setu. The general administration department has deputed the 35 senior officials to oversee arrangements and coordinate between departments. They will be stationed in Vaishali from November 17 until the conclusion of the Prime Minister’s visit. The deployment is intended to ensure that preparations are completed on time and that the programme is conducted smoothly, according to the report. A review meeting was held at Jafarpatti in Rajapakar block to assess the progress of preparations. Deputy Chief Minister Bijendra Prasad Yadav, BJP state president Sanjay Saraogi and JD(U) state president Umesh Singh Kushwaha attended the meeting and inspected the venue. Officials briefed the leaders on the arrangements and were directed to complete the remaining work within the stipulated timeframe. The bridge is among the key infrastructure projects linked to the visit. The Kachchi Dargah-Bidupur crossing is a six-lane structure over the Ganga, connecting the Patna-side Kachchi Dargah area with Bidupur in Vaishali district. Its formal opening is expected to add a major river-crossing link to the region’s road network, although the report does not provide details of traffic operations, tolling, access roads or the project’s construction cost. The Jandaha-Rajapakar industrial area is also scheduled to be inaugurated. The report does not specify its total area, investment commitments, industries planned or the number of jobs expected. Both projects are being presented as part of a wider set of development initiatives and projects that the Prime Minister is expected to unveil for Bihar during the visit. Alongside the administrative preparations, NDA constituents met at the JD(U) state headquarters to coordinate the political mobilisation. The meeting was attended by Umesh Singh Kushwaha, Sanjay Saraogi, LJP (Ram Vilas) state president Surendra Vivek, HAM-S state president Anil Kumar and RLM acting state president Prashant Pankaj. The alliance leaders discussed booth-level coordination, mutual understanding among the constituent parties and the management of workers for the programme. They also thanked Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary for naming the bridge after former chief minister and JD(U) president Nitish Kumar, describing the proposed inauguration as a matter of pride and joy for Bihar. The immediate administrative milestone is the deployment of the 35 senior officials in Vaishali from November 17. Preparations will continue until the Prime Minister’s scheduled visit and the proposed inauguration of Nitish Setu and the Jandaha-Rajapakar industrial area on November 21. Share Copy URL

national_raw_news.title: No Compromise on Devotees’ Safety: CM Yogi Directs Officials to Ensure Elaborate Chhath Arrangements
national_raw_news.content: Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath on Friday directed officials to ensure comprehensive arrangements for the safety, convenience and cleanliness of devotees during Chhath Mahaparva, stressing that there would be no compromise on public safety and essential facilities at ghats across the state. Chairing a high-level review meeting through video conferencing, the Chief Minister instructed district administrations to complete all preparations well in advance, particularly in districts expected to witness large gatherings, including Varanasi, Gorakhpur, Ballia, Azamgarh, Ghazipur, Lucknow, Ghaziabad, Basti and Kanpur Nagar. Describing Chhath as a festival rooted in faith, discipline, purity and gratitude towards nature, Adityanath said lakhs of devotees would participate in the celebrations across the state. He noted that devotees would offer arghya to the setting Sun on the evening of November 15, while the four-day festival would conclude on November 16 with prayers and offerings to the rising Sun. The Chief Minister directed officials to inspect all major ghats, rivers, ponds and other water bodies and ensure proper cleaning, adequate lighting, accessible approach roads, drinking water facilities, toilets and changing rooms for women. Emphasising devotees’ safety, he ordered the installation of strong barricades and warning signboards at vulnerable locations after assessing water levels and depths. Adequate numbers of trained divers, boats and water police personnel must be deployed to prevent accidents, while CCTV cameras and public address systems should be installed for surveillance and crowd management, he said. Adityanath also called for special arrangements for women, children and senior citizens, directing authorities to deploy sufficient police personnel, including women officers, at major ghats. He asked police personnel to discharge their duties with restraint, sensitivity and a cooperative approach. District-level control rooms and effective coordination between police and administrative officials should also be ensured, he added. The Chief Minister directed officials to prepare traffic management plans, identify necessary diversions and designate parking areas in advance to prevent congestion around puja sites. In view of the festival-related travel rush, Adityanath instructed the Uttar Pradesh State Road Transport Corporation to operate additional buses from Delhi to various districts of eastern Uttar Pradesh. He also directed officials to ensure that passengers were not charged fares above the prescribed rates. The Urban Development and Panchayati Raj departments were asked to organise special cleanliness drives around ghats and ensure uninterrupted power supply, with alternative lighting arrangements wherever necessary. The Chief Minister further directed authorities to ensure the availability of first-aid camps, ambulances and emergency services at major puja sites. Warning against negligence, Adityanath reiterated that cleanliness, safety and public convenience must remain the top priorities during the festival. Senior officials were also instructed to personally inspect the arrangements and seek the assistance of Civil Defence, NCC and NSS volunteers to ensure the smooth and safe conduct of Chhath Mahaparva. (IANS Inputs)
